item.title: Abiodun pledges more development for Remoland
item.description: .as Odemo seeks ₦600m for palace reconstruction, highlights security gains, attracts investors to Isara By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the development of Remoland, pledging sustained investments in infrastructure, healthcare, education and economic growth as his tenure gradually winds down. Abiodun also assured the people of Isara-Remo that his administration was working towards establishing a legacy hospital in the community to improve access to quality healthcare and strengthen the delivery of medical services in the area. The governor gave the assurances on Saturday at the 57th Afotamodi Day Festival held in Isara-Remo, Ogun State. The celebration, themed “Preserving Our Heritage, Restoring Our Glory,” also featured a fundraising initiative for the reconstruction of the palace of the Odemo of Isara-Remo, Oba Peter Oluwole Ogunbayo, with an estimated target of N600 million. Speaking through the State Commissioner for Environment, Mr Ola Oresanya, Abiodun described the annual festival as more than a cultural gathering, noting that its 57-year history had established it as an enduring symbol of the identity, traditions and collective aspirations of the Isara people. “For 57 years, this festival has remained a powerful symbol of the history, values, traditions and collective identity of the Isara people,” he said. The governor noted that the festival had continued to provide a platform for preserving the community’s cultural heritage, strengthening family bonds, promoting religious harmony and fostering unity among residents. He commended the Afotamodi Planning Committee, traditional institutions and other stakeholders for initiating the palace reconstruction project, urging Isara indigenes at home and abroad to support its successful completion. According to him, the palace represents far more than a physical structure, as it embodies the authority of the traditional institution, cultural continuity and the collective dignity of the community. “A palace is not merely a physical structure; it is an enduring symbol of traditional authority, cultural continuity, communal pride and the dignity of the institution it represents,” Abiodun stated. On his administration’s development agenda, the governor assured the people that efforts to bridge infrastructure gaps and improve transportation networks across rural and urban communities would be sustained. He disclosed that plans were being advanced for a legacy hospital in Isara-Remo, describing the proposed facility as a strategic investment in the health and wellbeing of the people. He said the hospital, when completed, would improve access to medical services, create employment opportunities and serve as a lasting social investment in the community. item.title: Sex agreement should be part of marriage contract
item.description: By Olaosebikan Olaniyi Marriage is a contract, and every serious contract should be explicit about its most important terms. Sex is central to marriage. It affects emotional bonding, physical health, fidelity, and long-term satisfaction. Leaving it to assumptions and unspoken expectations is why so many marriages fail. A sex agreement as part of the marriage contract makes sense for three clear reasons. 1. It Creates Clarity and Honesty Most couples never have an honest conversation about their sexual needs, boundaries, frequency, and values before marriage. They assume love will handle it. A formal agreement forces that conversation. It allows both partners to state what they want, what they do not want, and what is non-negotiable. Clarity before marriage prevents resentment after marriage. 2. It Protects Consent and Mutual Respect Marriage does not equal automatic consent. A sex agreement affirms that both partners have ongoing rights over their own bodies. It can define consent, right to say no without punishment, agreement on fidelity, protection, and respect for periods of illness, pregnancy, stress, or trauma. This protects both husband and wife and builds a culture of respect, not entitlement. 3. It Prevents Future Conflict Many divorces and infidelity cases stem from sexual incompatibility and unmet expectations. One partner wants sex daily, the other weekly. One sees pornography or open marriage as acceptable, the other does not. One wants children immediately, the other wants to delay. If these issues were agreed upon in writing as part of the marriage contract, couples would either resolve them early or realize they are not compatible before making a lifelong commitment. Including a sex agreement does not make marriage less romantic. It makes it more mature. We sign agreements for money, property, and children. Why should we ignore the very act that creates children and sustains intimacy? Marriage should include a clear, mutual, and voluntary agreement about sex. It is practical, it is respectful, and it is necessary for a healthy modern marriage. Lack Of Sex Is The Biggest Damage In Marriage Many things can damage a marriage like money problems, bad communication and family interference. But none damages a marriage faster and deeper than lack of sex, it is more easy for a marriage to crash when she’s always tired of handling room affairs or when he’s busy pursuing dreams forgetting the importance of marital satisfaction. Ma’am, you’re not a nanny, you’re a wife, no domestic assignment in the house should be paramount than attending to your husband’s sexual life, SEX is the main reason why you’re married, sex is why you said I do and should be prioritized. Sex is not just physical pleasure. Sex is the bond that separates marriage from every other relationship. You can talk to a friend, share money with a brother, and laugh with a colleague. item.title: Hidden Curriculum of Leadership: What does the environment teach leaders?
item.description: By Dayo Oyinlola Institutions are ecosystems made up of individual units that live in symbiotic relationships with each other. In these environments, information is processed dynamically and learning occurs both formally and informally. We must consider this reality when discussing leadership development. Leaders learn through written documents and institutional codes of conduct: values, laws, behavioral manuals, KPIs and OKRs that organisations establish to hold leaders accountable. And then there are the experiences nobody formally teaches, but everyone learns. A young executive watches how decisions are made. They notice who gets rewarded and who gets overlooked. They observe what happens when someone challenges authority, misses a target, refuses to compromise or asks an uncomfortable question. Nobody necessarily sits them down to teach these lessons. We often think of leadership development as something that happens through formal training, coaching, mentoring and experience. All of these matters, but leaders are also continuously shaped by the systems, institutions, cultures and circumstances within which they operate. And sometimes, the lessons being taught by the environment are very different from the lesson’s organisations believe they are teaching. Consider an organisation that claims to encourage employees to challenge ideas, yet senior leaders consistently dismiss people who disagree with them. Employees then learn that deference is safer than speaking up. Over time, people respond to what they experience rather than what they are told. The environment teaches what is rewarded. It teaches what is tolerated. It teaches how power works, whose voice matters and whether speaking up is valued or punished. It teaches people what leadership really means when it is exercised, not what the organisation says leadership means. This becomes particularly important in difficult operating environments. But there is another question worth asking: What happens when the environment consistently makes the wrong behaviour easier than the right one? If people repeatedly experience an environment where ethical behaviour is punished and unethical behaviour is rewarded, the environment itself becomes part of their leadership development. This is why integrity cannot survive indefinitely as an individual act of courage. For it to become sustainable, it must become part of the collective environment. For leaders operating in contexts where regulatory uncertainty, infrastructure gaps, talent shortages, limited access to capital and complex stakeholder expectations are part of the reality, this distinction becomes even more important. These realities do not excuse poor leadership. But they shape the choices leaders have to make. Leaders therefore need the ability to understand the forces around them without becoming defined by them. item.title: It’s time for results, by Funmi Komolafe
item.description: Beloved, it is mid November already. Some are counting the number of days left for 2026 to roll away; others are counting down towards political events in their country. As a Christian what is the focus of your count down? Yours should be a count down to the physical manifestation of your miracle; it should be a count down to the expiration of a challenge in your life. In other words, the count down to the end of 2026 should be for a Christian the time to celebrate results. The one that would celebrate would not give up. However, as human being, we tend to feel disappointed when we have not been able to attain the goals that we set for ourselves. Beloved, lamentations, wearing mournful looks, depression, suicide attempts, all of these do not produce positive results. These expressions should not be associated with a Christian that has deep faith in God and the ability of God to meet all needs. Philippians 2 vs. 13-16 ( KJV) tells us : “ For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure. Do all things without murmurings and disputings: That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world; Holding forth the word of life; that I may rejoice in the day of Christ, that I have not run in vain, neither labored in vain”. This passage simply tells us that when we refuse to allow challenges to weigh us down, the Holy Spirit would be active in us and the result would be joy. The Holy Bible gives us a firm warning about complaints, murmurs and the like in 1st Corinthians 10 vs. 10: “ Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer”. A deeper understanding of this passage is that complaints, murmur delight Satan and his demons. It draws one away from God and draws one closer to the enemy that would eventually, destroy and terminate life. Remember, the words of our Lord Jesus in John 10 vs. 9 & 10: “I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture. The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly”. So, Brethren, you need to make a choice between holding on to faith and hope in God, or you allow yourself to be destroyed by thoughts of suicide, frustrations, tears etc. However, we are here to lift up faith at a time like this and not to encourage anyone to give up. item.title: I don’t want to be stereotyped because of my looks – Obioma Ofoegbu
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Obioma Ofoegbu has spoken about the challenges of being stereotyped because of her plus-size physique, saying she is determined to establish herself as a versatile performer capable of taking on diverse roles. In an interview with Potpourri, Ofoegbu said she had repeatedly been offered roles that portrayed her as an older woman or confined her to characters typically associated with plus-size actresses. “My biggest challenge when I started was not being stereotyped because of my body type. A lot of times, they tried to give me roles just because I’m a plus-size woman. They would make me older in some movies or give me the same stories that a plus-size woman is expected to tell,” she said. The actress, who officially began her film career in 2020 after years of participating in stage plays and theatre productions during her school days, said she had rejected several roles in a bid to break away from such limitations. “I’m young. I don’t have to play an older woman or a married woman just because I’m plus-size. I don’t want to be placed in a box because of my looks, my appearance, or where I live,” she added. Speaking about her most challenging role, Ofoegbu identified her performance in Africa Magic’s series, The Low Priest, where she portrayed a villainous character who undergoes a transformation. She described the experience as physically demanding, revealing that she had to learn more Igbo, chant incantations and endure challenging filming conditions. The experience, she said, strengthened her confidence in her abilities and taught her that preparation and resilience could help her handle demanding characters. Despite her preference for diverse roles, Ofoegbu admitted that economic realities in Nigeria could make accepting stereotypical roles necessary, particularly for emerging actors trying to establish themselves financially. “I’m not a Funke Akindele yet. I’m not big enough to be producing as I please, so definitely I would take up those roles. I would grow as an actor, save, build and get my face out there,” she said. She also described acting as an uncertain source of income for emerging performers, advising actors to develop alternative income streams rather than depend entirely on film roles. On film promotion, the actress, who also has experience as an executive producer, maintained that actors should support projects they feature in but insisted that producers must have independent marketing strategies. Her long-term ambition, she said, is to have her work recognised beyond Africa and collaborate with filmmakers across different parts of the world. “I’m an actor, I’m not just a Nollywood actor. I like to see myself as an actor. Nollywood is a starting point for me,” she said. The post I don’t want to be stereotyped because of my looks – Obioma Ofoegbu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Cut ties with ungrateful people, disloyal family members – Titilola Ajayi
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Rising actress and filmmaker, Titilola Ajayi, popularly known as Omoposh and known for her movie Mr and Mrs Parker, has stressed the importance of setting personal boundaries, urging people not to tolerate disrespect, exploitation or emotional manipulation, even from family members. Ajayi made this known in a recent post on her Instagram page, where she addressed the need to walk away from relationships with ungrateful people and disloyal family members. According to her, family relationships should never be used as an excuse to endure mistreatment. “Clear boundaries are important and honestly cutting ties with ungrateful people or disloyal family members is also valid. Family should never be an excuse to tolerate disrespect, exploitation or emotional manipulation,” she wrote. She also had a message for people who continue to show kindness, generosity and support to others despite unpleasant experiences. “To all the good hearted people who give , support and show up for others don’t let experiences change your beautiful heart. Continue to be kind but learn to set boundaries . You can have a good heart and still know when to cut off ingrates and walk away,” she added. item.title: Nollywood must stop choosing Instagram numbers over talent – Uche Montana
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Uche Montana has questioned the Nigerian movie industry’s growing emphasis on social media popularity over acting ability, insisting that talent should remain an important consideration in the selection of actors. She shared her thoughts during an interview with media personality Davibes Olamide, where she also discussed friendship, fame, success and the realities of celebrity life. Speaking about the industry’s preference for social media numbers, she said: “The Nigerian movie industry needs to stopnpicking numbers on Instagram over talent” The actress also shared her thoughts on the relationship between friendship and success. Asked if she would pursue success even if it meant losing her friends, Montana responded: “Without my friends would i be broke ?Because I don’t want to be broke” She further explained her position on the value of genuine friendship, stating: “You can’t quantify friendship with the things of the world . Because good friendship means the world” Addressing the misconceptions surrounding celebrity life, Montana identified the belief that celebrities receive things for free as one of the biggest lies about fame. “The biggest lie about being a celebrity is that you get things for free” She also pointed out that certain things remain beyond the reach of fame, saying: “One thing fame can’t buy is peace good health” On the subject of respect and personal value, she observed: “People only respect you when you have value” The post Nollywood must stop choosing Instagram numbers over talent – Uche Montana appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Odumodublvck set to make acting debut in TG Omori’s ‘The Rise of the Machine’
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Multi-award-winning rapper Odumodublvck is showcasing his artistic depth with a stellar performance in his acting debut in a short film directed by ace cinematographer TG Omori. On November 7 2026, rapper Odumodublvck and cinematographer TG Omori were special guests at the closing ceremony and award gala of the 15th Africa International Film Festival ( AFRIFF), where they screened their short film titled ‘The Rise of the Machine’. The film, directed by celebrated cinematographer TG Omori, who is famous for shooting some of Africa’s most iconic music videos of the past decade, will see Odumodublvck make his acting debut in a role that promises to unleash another dimension to his talent and creativity. Speaking on the short film in a recent interview on TVC, the rapper described it as an addendum to his recently acclaimed projects, ‘The Machine is Coming’ and ‘The Industry Machine’. On making his acting debut, the award-winning rapper shared that he has enjoyed acting from a young age and always wanted to showcase that talent. “Since I was in primary and secondary school, I was in drama club. And with movies, I can show a lot more than listening to my music might show.” The short film is a precursor to the release of his upcoming project of the same name, which will complete his Machine Trilogy. The first instalment, ‘The Machine Is Coming’ enjoyed huge commercial success with the hits ‘Legolas’ and ‘Pity This Boy’ featuring Victony. The album was recently nominated for the Best Rap Album and Album of the Year at the 18th Headies. The follow-up, ‘The Industry Machine,’ also spawned chart-topping records with the hit single ‘Industry Machine’ and the hip hop anthem ‘If You Like Gym,’ which earned the nod for Best Rap Single at the 16th Headies. ‘The Rise of the Machine’ was shot in Lagos State and marks a major chapter in the career of Omori, who will be making his movie directorial debut and Odumodublvck, who serves as co-producer and executive producer. The short film is scheduled for release later in 2026 ahead of Odumodublvck’s new project, which will complete his Machine Trilogy while also kicking off his career as an actor and filmmaker. item.title: Australian pop singer, Nishka set to make Lagos performance debut
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Australian pop singer, Nishka, is set to make her Lagos performance debut as a special musical guest at Escape, an upcoming art exhibition that will bring music and contemporary visual art together in Lagos on November 28, 2026. The Melbourne-based singer’s appearance at the exhibition, organised by visual artist Fortune Ileleji and Grammy-winning musician Tejiri Sonics, is expected to add an international dimension to the creative experience while introducing Nigerian audiences to Nishka’s distinctive blend of soulful vocals, contemporary pop and rhythm-driven production. For Nishka, the Lagos performance represents more than another appearance on the international music calendar. It marks the latest stage in the journey of an artist whose sound has been shaped by multiple cultures, genres and experiences. Raised in Melbourne, Australia, in a family of Macedonian heritage, Nishka grew up surrounded by soul, funk, hip-hop and house music, alongside the traditional sounds of her family background. Those influences would eventually become part of the musical foundation from which she developed her own identity in pop. Her journey into music began early. At 10, Nishka started singing while simultaneously taking up martial arts. For several years, she pursued both disciplines, competing in martial arts tournaments while developing her vocal ability. By the age of 15, however, she had made a decisive choice: music would become her life’s pursuit. Today, Nishka’s music combines a soulful voice with emotional storytelling and a strong rhythmic character. Her songs explore love, desire, vulnerability and self-discovery, shifting between intimate, emotionally charged moments and energetic, groove-driven sounds. Her debut single, On My Mind, offers an introduction to that musical identity, blending personal expression with a contemporary pop sound. The choice of an art exhibition as the setting for her first Nigerian performance is also significant. Music and visual art, though expressed through different mediums, often meet at the same point—the attempt to translate emotions, memories and experiences that words alone cannot fully capture. That intersection is at the heart of Escape. The exhibition will bring together the visual work of Fortune Ileleji and Tejiri Sonics, with Nishka’s live performance adding a musical layer to the experience and creating a platform where contemporary art and international pop music converge. For the organisers, the appearance of an Australian-based artiste also underscores the increasingly interconnected nature of the creative industries, where artists, audiences and cultural influences now move across borders with greater ease. For Nishka, Lagos offers another cultural setting in which to expand an artistic identity already built from different musical traditions. item.title: My appearance has helped with visibility, branding — DJ Pretty Smile
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Sexy and beautiful Nigerian disc jockey, Onyinyechi Maureen Eneje, popularly known as DJ Pretty Smile, has admitted that her physical appearance has played a significant role in boosting her visibility and personal branding, even as she insists that talent and performance remain the key to sustaining a successful career. The beautiful DJ, who made the revelation in an interview with Potpourri, said her personality and appearance often attract people’s attention initially, but her ability to deliver behind the decks is what keeps them interested. According to her, being a woman in a male-dominated entertainment industry comes with its advantages in terms of visibility, but appearance alone cannot guarantee longevity in the profession. “I think people are first attracted to my personality and appearance, but what keeps them interested is my energy and ability to actually deliver behind the decks. Being a woman in a male-dominated space definitely makes people notice you, but looks alone cannot sustain a career. You have to be good at what you do,” she said. She added that although her appearance has contributed to her visibility and branding, she wants to be recognised primarily for her musical abilities and capacity to entertain audiences. “My appearance has definitely helped with visibility and branding, but I’ve always wanted people to remember me as DJ Pretty Smile, the DJ who can actually make a room move,” she added. Speaking on why she chose disc jockeying over singing or dancing, Eneje said her passion for music and its ability to influence people’s moods informed her decision to become a DJ. “I’ve always loved music and the way it can change people’s mood instantly. I chose DJing because I love being the person who controls that energy and creates an experience for people,” she explained. She further described disc jockeying as more than simply playing songs, noting that the profession requires an understanding of audiences, timing and the ability to establish a connection with people. “For me, it’s not just about playing songs; it’s about knowing what people want to hear, when they want to hear it, and creating that connection with the crowd. I also love the freedom and creativity that comes with DJing,” she said. On the argument that disc jockeys do not receive the recognition and financial rewards commensurate with their contributions to the music industry, DJ Pretty Smile agreed that the concern was justified to some extent. She observed that DJs play an important role in promoting songs and introducing music to wider audiences, but their contributions are not always adequately recognised or rewarded. “To some extent, yes. DJs play a huge role in the music industry because we help introduce and push songs to audiences, but sometimes the recognition and financial rewards don’t reflect the value we bring,” she stated. item.title: I don’t just want a relationship, I want something meaningful – Peju Johnson
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Peju Johnson says her priorities in love and career have changed as she grows older, stressing that she is no longer interested in relationships merely for the sake of being in one but desires a meaningful union built on genuine love, peace, friendship and mutual understanding. The actress, who attracted attention on social media on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, as she celebrated her birthday with stunning photographs, made this known in a chat with *Potpourri*, where she reflected on her journey in the movie industry, personal struggles, love life and aspirations for the future. According to Johnson, her experiences in the entertainment industry have taught her patience, resilience and the importance of self-belief, particularly in an environment where not everyone who appears supportive genuinely wishes others well. “The film industry has taught me patience, resilience and the importance of believing in myself, even when nobody else sees the vision,” she said. “I’ve learnt that not everybody who smiles with you genuinely wants to see you win, and that’s okay. You must learn to protect your peace, stay focused and never allow people’s opinions to define your worth.” Speaking about her changing expectations in relationships as she advances in age, the actress said she now places greater value on emotional stability, intentionality and personal growth than simply having a romantic partner. “As I grow older, my priorities are becoming clearer. In my love life, I want peace, genuine love, friendship, understanding and a partner who is intentional. “I’m at a stage where I don’t just want to be in a relationship for the sake of being in one. I want something meaningful, something that adds value to my life and allows both of us to grow. “I want to love and be loved without losing myself in the process,” she stated. Beyond her expectations in love, Johnson said she is equally concerned about building a career and legacy that would extend beyond her achievements as an actress. She explained that her ambition goes beyond being recognised as an actress and producer, noting that she hopes to establish herself as a filmmaker and businesswoman capable of creating opportunities for others. “Career-wise, my major concern is building something that will outlive me. I don’t just want to be known as an actress and producer; I want to build a lasting legacy as a filmmaker, producer and businesswoman. “I want to create opportunities, tell meaningful stories and establish something that the next generation can benefit from,” she added. Reflecting on her greatest testimony as a woman, the actress attributed her journey and personal growth to God’s faithfulness, saying she had experienced difficult moments that required her to make tough decisions and find the strength to keep moving. “There are so many things I’ve been through that I cannot fully explain, but God has been faithful. item.title: Nigeria needs 700,000 housing units annually to tackle deficit, Durojaye says
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Chairman of the Board of Directors of Gateway Mortgage Bank Limited, Samuel Durojaye, has said that Nigeria needs to construct approximately 700,000 housing units annually over the next decade to significantly reduce its housing deficit. Durojaye noted that achieving the target would require sustained investment, improved access to housing finance and greater collaboration among key stakeholders in the real estate and mortgage sectors. Durojaye, who disclosed this at the 9th Annual General Meeting of Gateway Mortgage Bank Limited, held in Abeokuta, Ogun State described mortgage institutions as vital to bridging the country’s housing gap, explaining that they play a dual role in facilitating homeownership for individuals and providing property developers with access to the financing needed to expand housing construction. He stressed that strengthening mortgage financing would improve the capacity of developers to deliver more housing units and make homeownership more accessible to Nigerians. He added that increasing the supply of affordable housing would help ease pressure on the property market, particularly by moderating the persistent rise in rental costs across major urban centres. According to him, addressing the housing deficit requires a sustained focus on expanding housing supply and improving access to affordable financing to ensure that more Nigerians can secure decent and affordable homes. The chairman, however, identified access to long-term funding as one of the major constraints confronting mortgage banks, explaining that the long repayment periods associated with housing loans made it difficult for institutions to rely on short-term deposits. “The minimum tenure for a mortgage is 10, 15 or 20 years. You cannot take people’s money when they expect it back in 90 days and put it into a property that will not pay back until 15 years,” he said. He therefore called for funding arrangements that would align with the long-term nature of mortgage financing, stressing that sustainable access to capital was essential for expanding homeownership. Durojaye also urged Nigerians, particularly young professionals and salary earners, to embrace mortgage financing early in their careers, rather than commit substantial portions of their income to recurring rent payments. “Instead of paying ₦2m in rent every year, why don’t you buy a house and start paying ₦200,000 monthly from your salary?” he asked. He explained that mortgage arrangements enabled prospective homeowners to spread the cost of acquiring properties over an agreed period, allowing them to build long-term assets instead of continually spending on rent. To improve public awareness and encourage greater participation in the mortgage market, the chairman said the bank had intensified its enlightenment campaigns through radio programmes, engagements with market associations and interactions with civil society organisations. item.title: 2027: Group mobilises support for Tinubu, Yayi, Abiodun, APC candidates
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta A socio-development group in Ogun State, the IBD/Inumidun Squad, has commenced grassroots mobilisation for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the emergence of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, as governor of Ogun State in the 2027 general elections. The group also declared its support for Governor Dapo Abiodun and other candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC), urging residents of the state to participate actively in the forthcoming elections and vote for the party’s candidates. The convener of the group, Chief Ibrahim Dende Egungbohun, made the call at a mega rally helf in Abeokuta, which attracted members and supporters of the group, community leaders, political stakeholders and beneficiaries of his humanitarian interventions. The rally, according to the organisers, was part of efforts to strengthen the APC’s grassroots support base and galvanise political mobilisation across the state ahead of the 2027 general elections. Speaking with journalists on the sidelines of the event, Egungbohun expressed delight at the turnout, describing it as an indication of the confidence reposed in his leadership and the group’s community-based activities. “Standing here today at the historic Ake Palace and looking out at this sea of familiar, smiling faces, my heart is filled with profound gratitude and humility,” he said. He maintained that the large turnout went beyond ordinary political mobilisation, describing it as a reflection of the relationship the organisation had built with communities through its humanitarian activities. “The overwhelming turnout we are witnessing today goes beyond a mere political gathering; it is a clear demonstration of the genuine love our people have for our humanitarian efforts and, by extension, their confidence in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola,” he stated. Making a case for Tinubu’s re-election, the convener argued that a second term would enable the President to consolidate his administration’s economic reform programme and allow Nigerians to reap its anticipated benefits. “We must look at the bigger picture of our nation’s economic journey. Securing a second term for President Tinubu is going to be of immense economic importance to the generality of Nigerians, as it ensures the continuity and full maturation of the bold reforms needed to stabilise and grow our economy,” Egungbohun said. On the political future of Ogun State, he declared the group’s support for Senator Adeola’s anticipated governorship ambition, expressing optimism that his emergence as governor in 2027 would accelerate infrastructural development and human capital investment across the state. item.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
item.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday carried out the first-ever recovery of a spaceship, pulling off a successful “catch” of its Starship vessel as it returned to its launch site after a day in orbit. The spaceship emerged from a cloudy sky after withstanding the extreme heat of re-entering the Earth’s atmosphere, and descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The feat marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems — a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of space flight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into cheers as the spaceship eased into its high-tech nest on the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. This time the Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters do. Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he added. ‘Giant swoosh’ The vessel’s path home was carefully mapped out by engineers. “If you want to get back to the east coast of Texas, you have to fly over the entire continent to get back there. So inevitably, you’re flying over land and we spend a lot of time figuring out the safest way to do that,” senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore said. Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a “giant swoosh maneuver” in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas’ Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east. Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars. US space agency NASA is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. On Saturday, Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and SpaceX. “It was almost magic… Making more believers by the day… one step closer to (the Moon),” he said on X. Refueling challenge Musk, the world’s richest person, has already revolutionized the space sector with the partially reusable Falcon rockets, which regularly launch satellites and carry astronauts to the International Space Station. item.title: Denmark hammer Ronaldo-less Portugal 4-1 in Nations League match
item.description: Portugal were hammered 4-1 by Denmark on Saturday, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo following the superstar forward’s retirement from international football. Rasmus Hojlund starred with a superb brace as Denmark moved into second place in Group A4 and closed in on a spot in the quarter-finals with a brilliant display in Braga. The Danes are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures. A draw against third-placed Norway on Tuesday, 3-1 winners over Wales earlier, will see Denmark through. Ahead of kick-off Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s number seven and his name on their jerseys. Fans held up a huge banner which read “Thank you captain” as the teams entered the field, while applause rolled around the stadium once the match clock hit seven. Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to establish world records for goals and appearances in international football, netting 146 times in 234 matches. The highlight of his international career was winning Euro 2016, but it ended badly when the 41-year-old fell out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over not being selected for a Nations League fixture in September. That row led to the five-time Ballon d’Or winner being handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese football federation and his subsequent retirement, and Portugal looked liked they needed prime Ronaldo in a dismal display. Denmark were the better team from the first minute and it was no surprise when the away team went in at the break thanks to Pierre-Emile’s Hojbjerg’s spot-kick in the 43rd minute. Hojlund lashed home a brilliant volley four minutes after the restart and seven minutes later left the home crowd shellshocked with a strike of which Ronaldo would have been proud, the Napoli striker skipping past Ruben Dias before crashing home a powerful shot from the edge of the area. Boos and whistles began to ring out at the Estadio Municipal when Joachim Andersen headed in the fourth, and Bernardo Silva’s late consolation effort barely dampened the discontent. Antonio Nusa opened the scoring for Norway just before the hour mark in Oslo with a fine low strike before Andreas Schjelderup tapped home a perfect low cross from Erling Haaland, who rounded off the scoring from the penalty spot two minutes from time. Wales briefly had hope of getting a result when David Brook’s chipped finish halved the deficit in the 79th minute, but Craig Bellamy’s team will finish bottom of the group and risk being relegated to League B. item.title: [VIDEO] Atiku Promises To Resume Oil Exploration In Kolmani, Revive Mabilla Power Project
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, has promised to resume oil exploration activities at the Kolmani oil field, which he said were suspended under the present administration. He also pledged to restore electricity subsidies and revive work on the abandoned Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project in the North-East. ﻿ Atiku made these promises during his presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State on Saturday. Speaking at the rally, he said, “I will restore electricity subsidies. I also promise to restore security in the North-East sub-region and the country at large. I further promise to continue oil exploration activities in Kolmani so that we can have additional sources of revenue.” On his part, Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign, Mr. Austin Akobundu, criticised what he described as the poor governance and misguided policy decisions of the present administration. “There is hunger in the land, and the man who will eradicate it is Atiku,” he said. In the last general election, Atiku secured a significant number of votes in Bauchi State while contesting on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). item.title: 2027: I’m For Any Coalition That Supports Tinubu’s Re-Election — Gov Eno
item.description: Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State has thrown his weight behind the Rainbow Coalition led by Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, saying that he will back any coalition that supports President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Eno stated this while fielding questions during a media chat on Saturday. “That Rainbow Coalition is simply saying that we support President Tinubu as the President,” he said. “If I will join and be a member of any coalition — whether it is rainbow, call it any name. Any coalition that the central point is supporting the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, I am for it.” The governor said that the relationship between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Akwa Ibom is “good on the ground”. Eno, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the APC after his defection from the PDP in June 2025, said the two parties had agreed to support Tinubu, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, and himself in the 2027 general elections. “I will work with all of them, and I think we are good on the ground in Akwa Ibom when it comes to PDP-APC relationship,” the governor said. “We have agreed on the fact that we are supporting the President, we are supporting the Senate President, we are supporting the governor, and we have our clear understanding about those things.” The Rainbow Coalition is spearheaded by Wike to galvanise support for the re-election bid of President Tinubu in 2027. But the coalition has faced opposition from leaders of the APC. In October, 2026, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma said that the Rainbow Coalition has no presence in the state. Speaking during the distribution of campaign vehicles under the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in the state, Uzodimma insisted that the APC would secure victory in the 2027 elections through organic votes. The governor maintained that the APC was the only recognised political party in the state and urged supporters to vote for the party’s candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Similarly, Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal told the minister to make his political position clear over his involvement with the coalition, insisting that he cannot simultaneously support the APC and other political parties. “Our message is very, very clear: be on one side, you can’t be on two sides. If you are in APC, please come out and support the APC, not you are supporting APC here, and you are supporting some other political parties somewhere else,” he said during an interview with Channels Television’s Inside Sources on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York in October. item.title: Forgive Me If You Didn’t See Me In The Hinterlands,’ Tinubu Tells Plateau Attack Victims
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has asked families affected by the deadly attacks in Anguwan Rukuba , in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State that left many killed and several injured in March 2026, to forgive him for not visiting the communities. ﻿ Tinubu spoke at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-Central presidential campaign rally in Jos on Saturday. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport. Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland. But I saw the devastation; I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people. “But since then, that has changed; we are forging together. He, however, assured residents that their communities would be rebuilt for those displaced to return home. Tinubu said too many lives had been lost to attacks in Plateau since 2001. He condoled with families who have lost loved ones to such attacks. Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), called for unity, saying speaking different languages should not lead to divisions. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau. “What we should be getting is prosperity, not havoc, not crisis. Our government is not elected to inflict wounds on one another or to bury people. We have to lift people up from penury to prosperity. “One thousand forest guards are undergoing training right now. You will feel them; you will see them. You will feel secure in your villages and communities,” he added. The President also said the surveillance cameras had been procured as promised. Tinubu assured the residents that his government his working to ease their suffering. A deadly attack in Anguwan Rukuba, in Jos North Local Government Area of the state in March, 2026, left at least 20 people killed and many others injured. On April 2, Tinubu met with the affected families at the Jos Airport, where he condoled with them and assured them that such an incident would not recur. ﻿ The President was criticised for not visiting the affected communities, but his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga , said that said the visit was affected by a scheduled meeting with the President of Chad. The post Forgive Me If You Didn’t See Me In The Hinterlands,’ Tinubu Tells Plateau Attack Victims appeared first on Channels Television .
